chunks: My father (rah) narrated to me from Abdullah bin Ja'far, from Muhammad bin Isa, from al-Qasim bin Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan bin Rashid, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said, 'Noorah is an amulet and purity for the body.'

key_terms.النُّورَه: Noorah (a specific type of amulet or protective charm)
key_terms.لِلْجَسَد: For the body (physical aspect of purity)

ai.seo_question: What is Noorah and what is its spiritual and physical significance according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-'Amal* attributes to Imam Ali the definition of 'Noorah' (often identified as the Surahs Al-Fatiha and Al-Ikhlas or specific divine names) as a 'spread-out light' and a purifier for the body. Historically, this reflects the Shia emphasis on *ta'wiz* (amulets) containing Quranic verses as legitimate means of seeking spiritual and physical protection, distinguishing them from superstition by grounding them in Prophetic tradition. The description of it as 'purifier' (*tahoor*) links the physical act of recitation or wearing with the spiritual cleansing of the soul.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rh) said that 'Abdullah bin Ja'far narrated to me, from Muhammad bin 'Isa, form al-Qasim bin Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan bin Rashid, from Abi Basir, form Abu 'Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
"Amir al-Mu'mineen (a.s.) said, “Noorah is an amulet and purity for the body.”"
